source.title: Using mass-balance principles to optimize nutrition of lettuce
source.authors: Noah James Langenfeld and Bruce Bugbee

system_design.system_type: Deep-water culture hydroponics in a glass greenhouse
system_design.cultivar_units: One cultivar community per container; the methods report n=1 container for each cultivar
system_design.solution_replacement_policy: Long-running zero-discharge treatments retained solution across harvests; Study 3 also included a solution-replacement treatment after each harvest.
system_design.replication_note: The source describes one eight-plant community per cultivar container. It does not document independently replicated reservoir units per cultivar/treatment sufficient for a treatment-level generalization.

experimental_unit_audit.source_author_pseudoreplication_note: The article explicitly says plotted statistics were tested among pseudoreplicates (n=3 cultivars) and calls for future replication to eliminate pseudoreplication.

environmental_envelope.wue_assumption_context: The refill recipe used a WUE of 3 g dry biomass per litre transpired water; the article describes this as typical around 450 ppm CO2, 50% RH, daytime VPD ~1.5 kPa at 25 C. Actual WUE varied by cultivar and crop cycle.
environmental_envelope.elevated_co2_wue_note: The discussion cites that WUE in elevated-CO2 indoor environments can be as high as 6 g/L. This is not a direct elevated-CO2 treatment outcome in this experiment; it is a transfer challenge.

management_arms.policy: Mass-balance refill recipe, no nutrient solution replacement, repeated plantings
Adjusted mass-balance recipe to reduce accumulation of Ca/Mg/S/B/Cu while maintaining crop nutrition
Zero-discharge mass-balance solution retained across harvest cycles
Solution replacement after each harvest to reset EC
Independently replicated mass-balance recipe updated from per-loop tissue assays, transpiration and environmental data
Adaptive mass balance with residual-triggered independent ISE or laboratory sentinel assays

reported_results.yield_and_wue_difference_reported: The authors report no difference in yield, WUE or mass-balance recovery between zero-discharge and solution-replacement management in Study 3.

mass_balance_recovery.interpretation: Reported as 100 ±10% for most elements; the published abstract describes most elements above 90%.
Authors attributed over-recovery to zinc contamination in the fresh nutrient solution.
Low solution concentrations and analytical detection limits may affect recovery.
Large apparent deficit; authors discuss active uptake, precipitation and analytical limitations; mechanism not fully resolved.

reported_results.non_significant_control_result: Solution replacement after harvest did not significantly increase yield, WUE or nutrient uptake in the reported Study 3 comparison; the source does not demonstrate independent multi-reservoir treatment replication.

measurement_and_missingness.solution_assay_method: ICP-OES for elemental solution concentrations; nitrate-N by cadmium-reduction flow-injection analysis.
measurement_and_missingness.tissue_assay_method: Tissue digestion and ICP-OES; total tissue N by combustion. Plant tissues separated into roots, young leaves and (Study 3) mature leaves.
measurement_and_missingness.ph_control_input_accounting: pH control solution contributed N and, in early studies, S; these additions were included in the source's N input calculation and must remain part of every replication ledger.
source_reported_missing_or_estimated_val: Mature leaf tissue was not analyzed in Studies 1 and 2.
In Study 3, mature leaf tissue was not analyzed for the first harvest due to a harvesting error and estimated from later plantings.
Study 3 solution was not analyzed after the third harvest and was interpolated between the second and fourth plantings.
boundary_caveats: The study used one container per cultivar community (n=1) and explicitly recognizes pseudoreplication.
The 56 L reservoir has a high solution-volume-to-cultivation-area ratio and high nutrient buffering; this differs from smaller-volume systems.
Actual DLI ranged 25–40 mol m^-2 d^-1, which the authors state is higher than typical commercial production.
Relative humidity was not controlled and averaged 50% ±20%; VPD varied.
Zero liquid discharge does not independently prove zero gaseous nutrient loss or complete elemental closure.
Substrate adsorption/desorption and NFT hydraulics were not tested in this DWC experiment.

replication_requirements: Use multiple independently controlled reservoir loops per treatment and cultivar; determine count with pilot variance and prospective power analysis.
Treat plants as subsamples within a reservoir and crop cycles as repeated measures.
Randomize treatment across independent reservoirs and block by chamber/rack/environment.
Use at least one held-out cultivar × environment combination for transfer evaluation.
Pre-register one primary treatment contrast, minimum useful effect and non-inferiority limits for yield and tissue adequacy.
Measure DLI, VPD, CO2, temperature, transpiration and dry biomass; do not assume WUE remains 3 g/L outside its qualified envelope.
Account for all pH dosing, fertilizer, source-water, sample, tissue, residual, purge and discharge streams by element.
Measure roots, young leaves and mature leaves for whole-plant nutrient accounting where biologically appropriate.
Preserve ICP-OES / laboratory reference assays, ISE calibration, detection limit, uncertainty and raw trace.
Retain apparent over-recovery, under-recovery and unknown fractions as diagnostic residuals; do not relabel them as plant uptake.
Do not claim food safety or microbial containment from nutrient mass balance.
claim_ceiling: Published single-greenhouse DWC result with one container per cultivar community and source-reported long-run cycles. The fixture is a literature audit and replication requirement, not independent proof of generalizable multi-facility zero-discharge performance.
